=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1590-1592 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The re-ask branch `if ! unblock_ask_model; then ... reason=ask_failed; return 0; fi` gives the wrong reason; `unblock_ask_model` returns non-zero only on a context-build failure (line 1848) or a Claude capacity wait (rc=80, lines 1902-1906), while real model, isolation and parse failures (lines 1908-1911, 1920-1923, 1988-1992) return 0 and are logged as `refused_after_reask reason=other`.
  WHY: All four reviewers rate this NIT: the `return 0` control flow is correct and mirrors the first ask at line 1554, but the contractual `UNBLOCK_JUDGE` log line records a refused verdict for a deferral or context failure, and real model failures appear as `reason=other`.
- agents.d/7742-unblock-sandbox-instructions.md:5 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The Stable log prefixes bullet says `reason=ask_failed` means "the re-asked model call itself failed", but the code only logs `ask_failed` for a capacity wait or a context-build failure; real model or isolation failures are logged as `reason=other`.
  WHY: Anyone grepping logs or the stable-prefix contract for re-ask model failures will search for `ask_failed` and miss the real failures logged as `other`; the control flow itself is correct (NIT).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1587-1592 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `return 0` in the re-ask `ask_failed` branch exits before the `invalid_verdict` handling after the while loop, so no `ai:unblock-wait:v1 item=<n> reason=invalid_verdict` marker is posted, while other validation failures do fall through to it.
  WHY: The reviewer says skipping the marker could stall the project indefinitely; it rated two of its three related items MAJOR and one NIT, so the highest (MAJOR→high) is used here; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash state this `return 0` is by design (it mirrors line 1554 and the #7370 rule of no marker on a capacity wait).
- tests/test_unblock_judge.py:~3684-3835 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: No test covers the re-ask `ask_failed` branch at scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1590-1592, and the `_judge()` fixture has no hook to make `unblock_ask_model` return non-zero on the second call only.
  WHY: A regression that removes the log line or reorders the `return 0` would pass CI, even though the agents fragment documents `ask_failed` as a contractually observable reason (all three rate it NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "On a second failure, log `op=instruction_sandbox_check outcome=refused_after_reask reason=<id>` and fall through to the existing `invalid_verdict` handling unchanged."
  expected_change_site: scripts/unblock_judge.sh validation loop and the agents fragment bullet that describes the same
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The added `ask_failed` path runs `return 0` immediately, which bypasses the `invalid_verdict` logic after the `while` loop and so the `ai:unblock-wait:v1` marker is never posted (the reviewer rated it BLOCKER; anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly reject this gap as invalid).
- requirement: "On a second failure, log `op=instruction_sandbox_check outcome=refused_after_reask reason=<id>` and fall through to the existing `invalid_verdict` handling unchanged." plus the done-when clause on the re-ask and the `UNBLOCK_INSTRUCTION_SANDBOX_CHECK_ENABLED=false` kill switch
  expected_change_site: tests/test_unblock_judge.py — coverage of the re-ask `ask_failed` branch in scripts/unblock_judge.sh lines 1590-1592
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `test_judge_logs_reason_other_when_the_reask_fails_for_another_reason` covers only `reason=other`; the other branches have dedicated tests (`test_judge_reasks_once_when_instructions_need_network`, `test_judge_falls_back_to_invalid_verdict_after_a_second_refusal`, `test_judge_sandbox_check_kill_switch`), but no test exercises `if ! unblock_ask_model; then ...; return 0; fi`, and `_judge()` has only `MOCK_UNBLOCK_JUDGE_JSON` / `MOCK_UNBLOCK_JUDGE_JSON_REASK`, with no way to force a non-zero return.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- agents.d/7742-unblock-sandbox-instructions.md:line 5, the clause "`reason=ask_failed` when the re-asked model call itself failed"; scripts/unblock_judge.sh lines 1590-1592, lines 1908-1911 and 1920-1923, line 1992 (`return 0`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The documented meaning of `ask_failed` does not match the code: `unblock_ask_model` returns non-zero only on a context failure (line 1848) or a Claude capacity wait (line 1906, rc 80); a model or isolation failure writes `{}`, returns 0, and is logged as `refused_after_reask reason=other` followed by the `invalid_verdict` marker.
  WHY: Log greps for re-ask model failures will look for `reason=ask_failed` while the real failures appear as `reason=other`; the control flow is correct (`return 0` matches line 1554 and the #7370 rule of no marker on a capacity wait).
- tests/test_unblock_judge.py:the new test `test_judge_logs_reason_other_when_the_reask_fails_for_another_reason`; no test covers scripts/unblock_judge.sh lines 1590-1592 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `ask_failed` branch is untested, and the fixture has no hook to force a context failure on the second call only.
  WHY: Nothing fails today, but a later change that drops the log line or posts an `invalid_verdict` marker on a capacity wait would not be caught.
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE. The reviewer rejects the pass-1 gap: the second-refusal path (lines 1580-1583 → line 1595) does post the marker, and `ask_failed` is a failed model call, not a refusal.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: reword agents.d/7742-unblock-sandbox-instructions.md line 5 so `ask_failed` means a capacity wait or context-build failure and `reason=other` covers a re-ask with no usable verdict (1 line; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

  WHY: When `unblock_ask_model` fails (e.g. a timeout), the branch logs `ask_failed` and returns 0, skipping the `invalid_verdict` handling and leaving a confusing log state.

  WHY: A failed re-ask should fall through so that an `ai:unblock-wait:v1 item=<n> reason=invalid_verdict` marker is posted and the project does not stall indefinitely.

  PROBLEM: Error logging in the re-ask loop is asymmetric about `invalid_verdict` marker creation.
  WHY: `ask_failed` exits the loop early and no marker is created, while other validation failures fall through to `invalid_verdict`.
- TASK_GAP | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  Requirement: "On a second failure, log `op=instruction_sandbox_check outcome=refused_after_reask reason=<id>` and fall through to the existing `invalid_verdict` handling unchanged."
  Expected change site: scripts/unblock_judge.sh validation loop and the agents fragment bullet that describes the same.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:lines 1590-1592 (the `if ! unblock_ask_model; then unblock_log ... reason=ask_failed; return 0; fi` block) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The meaning of the `ask_failed` reason is inverted: it fires only for `context_failed` (line 1848) and the Claude capacity wait (rc=80, line 1906), while real model or isolation failures return 0 (lines 1910, 1922), produce a `{}` verdict and are refused as `reason=other`; agents.d/7742-unblock-sandbox-instructions.md:4 documents it as "when the re-asked model call itself failed".
  WHY: Runtime behavior is correct (it mirrors line 1554), but log consumers keyed on `reason=ask_failed` will see capacity waits and context failures, never a true isolation failure, and the re-ask adds a misleading log line that did not exist before this PR.
- TASK_GAP | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Requirement: "On a second failure, log `op=instruction_sandbox_check outcome=refused_after_reask reason=<id>` and fall through to the existing `invalid_verdict` handling unchanged." plus the done-when clause (a mocked verdict with `git fetch origin main` is refused and re-asked once, and the second verdict is acted on; with `UNBLOCK_INSTRUCTION_SANDBOX_CHECK_ENABLED=false` the first verdict is accepted).
  Expected change site: tests/test_unblock_judge.py — coverage of the re-ask `ask_failed` branch in scripts/unblock_judge.sh lines 1590-1592
  Evidence of absence: `test_judge_logs_reason_other_when_the_reask_fails_for_another_reason` covers only `reason=other`; the other branches have tests, but `if ! unblock_ask_model; then ...; return 0; fi` does not, and `_judge()` has no fixture variable to make `unblock_ask_model` return non-zero.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: None (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1590-1592; unblock_ask_model returns 1 at 1846-1849 for context construction failure and 1902-1906 for Claude capacity wait, while ordinary model failures return 0 at 1908-1923. | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The re-ask caller treats every non-zero return as `ask_failed` and logs `refused_after_reask`, although those return paths are not a refused second verdict; ordinary model failures return zero and are handled as `reason=other`.
  WHY: A capacity wait or context construction failure is recorded as a refused verdict, and an actual model failure is recorded as a different validation failure, so the operational log misstates what happened.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
